title: Runbook Retention and Responder Onboarding Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This handbook defines how Redwood retains, reviews, and evolves operational runbooks and how we onboard new on-call responders. The goal is to keep runbooks current, searchable, and actionable so first responders can reliably restore service, collect evidence, and communicate with stakeholders and customers.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-facing services that are part of Redwood’s hosted, dedicated, and private offering surface.
- Includes: runbook authoring standards, review cadence, archival policy, responder onboarding checklist, runbook exam criteria during game days, and customer communication templates.

Objectives:
- Ensure runbooks solve the problem: clear intent, preconditions, steps to mitigation, rollback and verification, and post-incident evidence requirements.
- Reduce mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) by providing crisp, tested procedures.
- Preserve institutional knowledge and reduce single-person bus factor.

Key Definitions:
- Runbook: A Confluence page that documents an operational procedure for diagnosis, mitigation, and recovery for a specific service or class of incidents.
- First Responder: The on-call engineer who picks up the initial alert and runs the runbook.
- Runbook Owner: The engineer/team responsible for keeping the runbook accurate.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Runbook Owner: maintain, update, test quarterly. (Typically the primary service owner).
- On-call Lead: coordinates responder onboarding, maintains training materials and game day schedule.
- People Ops: tracks onboarding milestones and ensures training completions are recorded.
- SRE/Platform: provides templates, tooling, and runbook review support.

Runbook Authoring Standards (minimum):
1) Title: short, service-name + short-description (e.g., payments-authorization-high-latency).
2) Purpose: one-paragraph summary of what the runbook does and what to expect after executing it.
3) Preconditions / Signals: what alerts/metrics/logs indicate this runbook applies; list thresholds and runbook triggering PagerDuty symptoms.
4) Quick Stabilization Steps: 3–5 high-confidence steps that stop customer impact or queue growth.
5) Full Recovery Procedures: step-by-step commands, consoles, queries, and API calls to remediate.
6) Verification & Post-checks: exact metrics/queries to confirm restoration.
7) Rollback / Escape Hatches: steps for timed rollback if mitigation fails.
8) Evidence Collection: required artifacts to attach to incident (logs, stack traces, request IDs, time windows).
9) Owner & Last Test: owner name, last test date, link to test run notes.

Runbook Review Cadence and Lifecycle:
- Critical runbooks (customer-facing, SLA-affecting): review every 3 months.
- Important runbooks (internal degradation, partial impact): review every 6 months.
- Informational runbooks (maintenance tasks, infrequent): review annually.
- Retirement: If not exercised or updated for 18 months, flag for deprecation review.

| Runbook Class | Review Frequency | Acceptance Criteria | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Critical (SLO-affecting) | Quarterly | Runbook executed in a game day or live incident within 12 months; automated verification steps included | Service Owner |
| Important | 6 months | Contains test checklist and a linked test report | Service Owner |
| Informational | 12 months | Clear owner and retire criteria | Service Owner |

Review Workflow (numbered steps):
1. Automated reminder is pushed 30 days before due to the runbook owner and On-call Lead (Slack + email).
2. Owner updates runbook and runs a dry-run (can be a simulated query against production-like data) and records results.
3. Reviewer (SRE or peer owner) validates steps and signs off on the page with a review timestamp and notes.
4. If the owner does not respond within 14 days, the On-call Lead escalates to the service manager.

Responder Onboarding Checklist (for new on-call engineer):
1) Pre-hire: Ensure access requests are in flight (PagerDuty, Slack, Confluence, cloud consoles).
2) Week 0 - Orientation (people-ops + On-call Lead): policy read-through, escalation matrices, SLOs & runbook location.
3) Week 1 - Shadowing: two paid shifts shadowing primary responder (read-only).
4) Week 2 - Supervised Execution: pair on low-risk incidents and maintenance.
5) Week 4 - Solo-responding: limited scope (non-critical services) followed by a 1:1 debrief with On-call Lead.
6) Certification: complete a scored game day (see Game Day Rubric) and pass the onboarding exam documented on Confluence.

On-Call Handoff Checklist (end of shift):
- Active incidents: summarize status, next actions, any running mitigations, TTLs, and current owners.
- Open alerts: list noisy alerts and recent false-positive signatures.
- Recent changes: any deploys/infra changes in last 6 hours.
- Link to commit(s) or rollout IDs if applicable.
- Confirm contact points and escalation path.

Game Day Integration and Scoring Rubric:
- Goal: exercise runbooks and validate they are actionable under stress.
- Cadence: At least one service-level game day per quarter; targeted critical services monthly.
- Participants: Runbook Owner, 2+ responders, SRE reviewer, product on-call if customer impact scenario.

Scoring (numeric, pass threshold 80+):
- Readability & Navigation (20 points): can responders find the runbook and understand intent in <2 minutes.
- Execution Clarity (30 points): steps are actionable, commands/scripts exist and run without modification.
- Instrumentation & Verification (20 points): verification queries and dashboards validate restoration.
- Evidence Collection & Postmortem Inputs (15 points): runbook specifies required evidence fields.
- Time to Stabilize Simulation (15 points): simulated MTTR meets the service target.

Postmortem Evidence Template (to be completed during incident):
- Incident ID:
- Start / End timestamps (UTC):
- PagerDuty alerts & responders involved:
- Affected customer segments and regions:
- Root cause hypothesis (one-liner):
- Actions taken (timestamped):
- Verification artifacts (links to logs, traces, dashboards):
- Rollback decisions (yes/no + why):
- Follow-up owners & ETA for fixes:

Customer Communication Templates (examples) :
1) Initial customer-facing status (short):
Subject: [Redwood] Service Degradation — <service-name>
Body: We are investigating elevated errors affecting <feature> for a subset of customers in <region>. Engineers are actively diagnosing. We will send updates every 30 minutes or when we have new information. Impact: [brief impact statement]. Next update: <time>.

2) Post-incident summary (long):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident Report — <service-name> <YYYY-MM-DD>
Body: Summary: timeline, impact, root cause, mitigation steps, user-facing workarounds, and permanent fixes planned. Include the incident ID, link to full postmortem (internal), and the publicly consumable summary.

Operational Tooling & Conventions:
- PagerDuty: use service-based schedules; first 4 responders must have primary/secondary tags.
- Status page: short public messages; internal Slack #incident channel gets richer, timed updates and runbook links.
- Confluence naming: oncall/runbooks/<service-name>/<runbook-slug>. Always use the template provided under /templates/runbook-template.

Sample diagnostic snippet (for logs):
```bash
# Narrow time window and request ID
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /service/payments --start-time 1672531200000 --end-time 1672534800000 --filter-pattern "\"request_id\" = \"<REQ_ID>\""
```

Acceptance & Metrics (what success looks like):
- 95% of Critical runbooks have a review record in last 90 days.
- Onboarding completion (shadow -> certification) for new responders within 30 days.
- Game day pass rate >= 80% across critical services every quarter.

Escalation & Failure Modes:
- If a runbook fails during live incident and causes >30m delay to recovery, the runbook is marked for immediate rewrite + emergency game day.
- If owner unresponsive to scheduled review, ownership is transferred temporarily to SRE for emergency edits.

Appendix A — Runbook Template (copy/paste):
- Title:
- Owner & Last Test Date:
- Purpose:
- Signals / Alerts / Preconditions (with metric thresholds):
- Quick Stabilization Steps (1–5):
- Full Recovery Steps (detailed with commands):
- Verification Queries / Dashboards (links & queries):
- Evidence to attach to incident: [list of artifacts]
- Rollback / Escape Hatch:
- Test Notes (link to game day execution):

Appendix B — Onboarding Exam (pass criteria):
- Written: identify correct runbook for 6 simulated alerts (40%).
- Practical: execute a low-risk recovery during supervised game day (40%).
- Oral: walk an On-call Lead through evidence collection and communication template (20%).

Contact & Ownership:
For questions about this handbook or to propose changes, contact the On-call Lead (oncall-lead@redwoodai.com) or the People Ops runbook steward.
